## Q1
The UGC has given a 10-point scale for grading. Arrange the following grades from highest to lowest performance.<br>
A. F<br>
B. P<br>
C. O<br>
D. A<br>
E. Ab<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q1 - Options
(A) B, A, D, E, C
(B) C, D, B, A, E
(C) A, D, C, B, E
(D) E, A, B, D, C

## Q1 - Hint
**Answer:** B
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q6

On the University Grants Commission letter-grade scale the grades run, from best to worst performance, Outstanding, then Excellent, then Very Good, then Good, then Average, then Pass, then Fail, and finally Absent. Among the grades listed here that ordering places Outstanding first, then grade A, then Pass, then Fail, then Absent. Matching those grades back to the given labels produces the sequence C, D, B, A, E, so the second option is correct.

## Q2
The NPE 1986 envisaged setting up residential schools with the aim of providing excellence coupled with equity and social justice. This led to the establishment of:

## Q2 - Options
(A) Kendriya Vidyalayas
(B) Navyug Schools
(C) Navodaya Vidyalayas
(D) Eklavya Residential Schools

## Q2 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q13

Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas were created under the National Policy on Education 1986 as pace-setting residential schools for talented rural children, combining excellence with equity. Kendriya Vidyalayas predate 1986 and serve transferable central employees; Eklavya schools are for tribal students under a later scheme.

## Q3
Select the correct statements pertaining to NEP 2020.<br>
A. It promotes secular and minorities education vehemently.<br>
B. It promotes multiple-entry–multiple-exit in higher education.<br>
C. It recommends that the state must spend 10 percent of GDP on education.<br>
D. It affirms that Sanskrit has more literature than Latin and Persian.<br>
E. It promotes private philanthropic education.<br>
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

## Q3 - Options
(A) A, B and C
(B) C and D
(C) B, D and E
(D) A and E

## Q3 - Hint
**Answer:** C
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jun 2026 (22 Jun, Shift 2) · Paper 1 · Q21

NEP 2020 introduces multiple entry and exit points in higher education (B), states that Sanskrit literature is larger than that of Latin and Greek/Persian (D), and encourages private philanthropic participation in education (E). It recommends 6% of GDP (not 10%), so C is wrong, and it does not frame itself in the terms of statement A.

## Q10
Assertion (A): Higher Education Institutions in the country with appropriate credit transfer mechanisms are facilitating students to enroll themselves in pre-designed academic programmes.<br>
Reason (R): Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) works on the principle of multiple entry-multiple exit as well as anytime, anywhere and any-level learning.

## Q10 - Options
(A) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
(B) Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
(C) A is correct but R is not correct.
(D) A is not correct but R is correct.

## Q10 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2026 (2 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q16

The Academic Bank of Credits supports portable, accumulated credits and flexible pathways including multiple entry and exit. That flexibility does not imply that institutions are facilitating enrolment only in pre-designed programmes, so the Assertion is false while the Reason is true.

## Q21
Match List I with List II:

| List I (Scholar) | List II (Field of Expertise) |
|---|---|
| A. Brahmagupta<br>B. Kautilya<br>C. Patanjali<br>D. Charaka | I. Political Strategist<br>II. Yoga<br>III. Physician<br>IV. Mathematician |

## Q21 - Options
(A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
(B) A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
(C) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
(D) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

## Q21 - Hint
**Answer:** D
**Topic:** Higher Education System
**Source:** UGC NET Jan 2025 (6 Jan, Shift 1) · Paper 1 · Q27

Matching ancient Indian scholars with their primary field of expertise:

- **A. Brahmagupta — IV. Mathematician:** Ancient Indian mathematician and astronomer who authored the *Brahmasphutasiddhanta* (628 CE), introducing the rules for arithmetic operations using zero and negative numbers.
- **B. Kautilya (Chanakya) — I. Political Strategist:** Prime minister to Chandragupta Maurya and author of the celebrated political and economic treatise *Arthashastra*.
- **C. Patanjali — II. Yoga:** Ancient sage and philosopher who compiled the foundational classical text of Raja Yoga, the *Yoga Sutras*.
- **D. Charaka — III. Physician:** Legendary ancient physician and one of the principal contributors to Ayurveda, author of the foundational medical treatise *Charaka Samhita*.

Matching sequence: **A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III**, which corresponds to **Option D**.
